0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 20 March 1962, after the draft finalized by the Dairy IndUitry Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 The need for standardization of cylindrical pipettes for bacteriological examination of milk has been felt by scientific workers and manufacturen of glassware. This ItaAdard coven the requirements of cylindrical pipettes commonly used in bacteriologic-.t examiftatieD otmilk. 03 In the preparation of this standard, apistance has been derived from the following publications:

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of t~st for cylindrical pipettes, calibrated for delivered capacity, suitable for bacteriological examination of milk.

2. CAPACITY
2.1 Cylindrical delivery pipettes for bacteriological examination of milk shall be of the following six capacities: a) b) c) d)

3. DEFINmON OF CAPACITY
3.1 The capacity corresponding to any graduation mark is defined as the volume of water at 27�0, expressed in millilitres, delivered by the pipette at 27�0, when emptied as described in Appendix A_

7. PACKING AND MARKING
7.1 The pipettes shall be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the vendor.

7.2 Each pipette shall have permanently and legibly marked on its surface, the following information:
a) Maker's name or registered trade-mark, if any; b) Nominal capacity followed by letters' ml'; c) Letters C D 27�0 t to indicate that the pipette is calibrated for delivery at 27�0; d) Delivery time; e) Inscription' Milk Bact'; f) The inscription' Ref to IS: 2025-1962' (SI' Note); and g) Batch or code number.
NOTa - U oder the Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks) Act, 1952 Section 6 (b). the abbreviation � IS I cannot be used without the previous ~ission of the Indian Standards IllIti&ution. Manufacturen intcnding to usc this marking should. thereforef obtain luch pertnillion from and register their names with the Indian Stand� � rda lnatltution.

7.2.1 The pipettes may also be marked with the lSI Certification Mark.
NOTE - The use of the lSI Certification Mark is governed by the prov.oOl of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Markl ) Act, and the Rulea and Ileguladona made thereunder. Presence of this mark on products covered by an Indiab Standard conveya the &Durance that they have been produced to comply with the l'J!9uirementa of that Itandard, under a well-defined system of inspection. testing and quality control durin. production. Thia Iystem, which it deviled and supervised by lSI aDd o~tecl by the producer. bu the further safe~rd that the products u actually marketed are contin\l~~ly checked by lSI for conformity to the Itandard. Details otconditiona, under whilb a licence for the uae of the lSI Certification Mark may be ,ranted to maowaeturen or procason, may be obtained from the Indian Standards IJailitudon.

APPENDIX A (Clause 3.1 )
DETERMINATION OF CAPACITY OF PIPBTTES A-I. PIlOCBD1JIlB A-l.1 Clean the pipette thoroughly. Suck distilled water till the meniscus is a Utdeabove tile ~aduadon mark. Keep the water level at thisposition by Presainl the top of the pipette firmly by a finger. Wi~ off aU adhering wate.- from the jet en, or the pipette by clean dry cloth. Hold the pptte vertically and allow the menilcua to fall slowly by reIeu~ the fiDF preIIure. Allow the water to ftID out tiU the lowest point otthe meniaeua II

7

IS I 2025� 1962

in the horizontal plane containing the top edge of the graduation mark. Stop the outflow and touch the jet end to the inside of a clean beaker to remove any adhering drop at the jet.
""1.2 Place a clean, taIId, suitable weighing bottle beneath the pipette and touch the tip of the jet of the pipette with the inside wall of the weighing bottle, holding it at a slightly inclined position. Remove the finger pressure from the top ofthe suction tube and collect the water in the stoppered bottle. Watch the meniscus till it stops moving, the jet remaining in contact with the inside wall of the bottle throughout and then remove the piFtte (no attempt shall be made to force out the water remaining in the Jet of the pipette}. Weigh the stoppered bottle with water and thus determine the weight of water delivered by the pipette. Note the temperature of the water, the air, the barometric pressure and calculate the volume of water delivered by the pipette at 27�0 by applying appropriate corrections. A-I.3 The pipette shall be taken to have satisfied the requirement if the volume of water 80 obtained is within the limits prescribed.

below. However, the p .rchaser and the vendor may agree to accept any other procedure.
11-1.2 Lot - All the pipettes-itt a single consignment belonging to the same type and drawn from the same batch of manufacture shall constitute a lot.

Bat.3 Samples shall be tested from each lot for ascertaining conformity of
the pipettes in the lot to the requirements of tltis specification.
8-1.4 A sample of forty-two pipettes shall be drawn from a lot. In case the lot size is less than 42, all the items in the lot shall be drawn. Random number tables shall be used for drawing the samples. If such random number tables are not available, the sample shall be drawn in the manner given below: Starting from anY'pipette in the lot, count them as 1, 2, :~, ... .etc, up to R in a systematic manner, where R is t.'iual to the integral part of A I . : . , N being the total number of pipettes in the lot. Every Rth pipette thus counted shall be separated until 42 pipettes are obtained from the lot to give sample for teat.

B-2. ClUTElUON POR CONFORMITY
8-2.1 Select at random two pipettes from the 42 pipettes for alkalinity test ( '" 5.2.1) and test them according to the method given in Appendix C. lfthe two pipettes pass the test, then only the remaining part of the sample shan be tested for conformity of the lot to the other requirements given in the specification. If the two pipettes fail in the test, no further test need be done and the lot shall be rejected

11-2.2 Ca~clty - Test the remaining 40 pipettes for capacity. accept the lot if no C:lefective is found and reject the lot if five or more defectives ar..
found. If, however, the number of defectives among the pipettes tested is between 1 and 4, the remainder of the lot shall be tested on hundred cent basis for the characteristic and all pipettes found defective shal be eliminated. Fol' lot sizes lea than 42, all the pipettes in the lot shall be tested and the pipettes found defective shall be eliminated,

rer-

11-2.3 VA� � lupeed. . -- Every pipette in the sample tested for capacity shall simultaneously be inspected for visual characteristics prescribed iD 5.2 to S.t and all pipettes found defective shall be eliminated and replaced by good ones.

B-2.t D...., TIiD. aacI DIm...I. . . - Tests for these characteristics . shall be carried out in stages by taking 8 pipettes at each stage out of the total number or 40, ait'd a decision taken in accordance with the directions given in 84A.l to 11-2.4.7 read with Table II. When a decisionis reached
9

IS I 2025 � 1962 after any stage of sampling, further pipettes shall be not tested. In case the lot size is less than 42, all the pipettes shall be tested for the characteristics and defectives eliminated.
8-2.4.1 The first stage of sampling shall constitute selection of 8 pipettes at random from the total number of 40 pipettes and testing 8 pipettes individually.
B-2.~.2 The lot cannot be accepted at the first stage even if there are no defectives, without further inspection.

APPENDIX C ( Clause 5.2.1 )
TEST FOR ALKALINITY C-I. APPARATUS

C-l.1 Erleameyer Flasks and CondeDsers - with ground-glass joints. Erlenmeyer flasks of 250-ml and 500-ml capacities; graduated flasks of 250-ml capacity.

0.1.2 Mortar - a suitable mortar made of steel. e-I.3 Te.t Sieves - two, one IS Sieve 40 and the other IS Sieve 60.
Non: - So long as the Indian Standard Test Sieves are not available, US Test Sieves or ASA Test Sieves of equivalent mesh sizes may be used (S', �IS: 460-1953 Specification for Test Sieves).

0-2. REAGENTS
C-2.1 Q,a811ty of -eaaeDt. - Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled water [SI' IS: 1070�1960 Specification for Water, Distilled ~uality ( R,vis,d )] shall be employed in te~ts.
NOTB - � Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities which affect the experimental results.

0.2.2 The following reagents are required. C.2.2.1 Sttmdtlrd HJdroehlorie Add Solulion - 0'01 N. Q.2.2.2 EtA,,1 Alcohol or R,clifi,d Spirit - (a) Ethyl alcohol 95 percent
by volume or (b) rectified spirit 95 percent by volume (conforming to IS: 323�1959 Rectified Spirit ( R,IJis,d) ].

C-U.3 Sta_d Sodiu", Hydro%id, Solution - 0�05 N.

0-2.2.4 M,,".1l RId Intliealor -- Dissolve 0-04 g of methyl red in 75 ml ethyl alcohol or rectified spirit_ Add 1'5 ml standard sodium hydroxide solution or a quantity sufficient to ensure that the colour of the solution corresponds to pH 5-2 and then dilute to 100 ml with water.
0.2.2.5 T,s' Solu'ion - Add 1-0 ml standard hydrochloric acid solution and 1-0 ml of methyl red indicator to about 240 ml of water. Bojl the solution for five minutes in an Erlenmeyer flask which has been previously tested in accordance with the test under c-3.1, cool the flask quickly under running water and make up the volume to 250 ml with water,

0-3. TESTING OF ERLENMEYER FLASK ASSEMBLY
c-3.1 Add 1-0 ml of the standard hydrochloric acid solution and 1�0 ml of methyl red indicator to about 240 ml of water, Boil the solution for five minutes in an Erlenmeyer flask of chemically resistant glass (a borosilicate glass of known type), cool the flask quickly under running water and make up the volume to 250 ml with water. Transfer 100 ml of the solution to the Erlenmeyer flask to be tested. Place the flask quickly in a bath of boiling water so that the level of the contained solution is below the level of water in the bath and attach a small reflux condenser. Continue boiling for one hour and at the end of this period observe the colour of the solution. Reject the flask if any change of colour of the test solution hu taken place. c-3.1.1 Erlenmeyer flask assemblies which have once passed the telt (II' c-3.1) for suitability -may. fail to do so iafter prolonged ItOraP. In such, a case they may be revived by washing with-five percent (wI,) solution of glacial acetic acid followed by washing with water until tree from acid, before use.
(M.

PROCEDURE

C'A.I Take sufficient number of pipettes to ~t 100 g of llul. Rinse thoroughly with water, dry in a stream of dry air and crush them in ,uch. manner that the particla pass through IS Sieve 60abut fail to p. . through IS Sieve 40. The crushing and sieving should be done in three 01 four stages to avoid too much fines. Spread the sieved particles, weighing in excess of 5 g, on a glazed paper and pus a ~t over them to remove any particles of iron which may have been introduced during crusDq. Wash the sieved glus free from dust in an Erleam~ flak with four successive 3O-ml portions of ethyl alcohol or rectified .pirit and day them at looo�2�C. Toe two Erlenmeyer flub (,., c.s.1) and traIIIfer exactly 51 of the sieved clean dry glals to one the flaIb. Transfer a lOO-Dil portion of the &ably pre~ test IOlation ( I" Q.2.2.5) to both the flut-s. Place the flub quickl1 in a bath of boiHng water 10 that ~he IeveII of the contained solutions are below the level of the water ill the bath aDd attach

or

12

IS :2025.1962
the previously tested reflux condensers, Keep the fla~ks in the boiJjn~ waterbath for 30 minutes and then take them out and enol quickly under running water. From the first flask containing powdered glass samples decant out the test solution into a third Erlenmeyer ftask. Add 4 ml of water to the powdered glass residue in the first flask, shake a little and decant out into the third flask, taking care to see that transference of the powdered glass is avoided as far as possible. Also add 4 ml of water to the second flask containing only the test solution (blank ). titrate the solution in the third flask immediately with the standard hydrochloric acid solution to the pink colour of the blank test solution in the second flask.

C.5. TITRE VALUE
0.5.1 Report tbe titre value as the number of millilitres of 0-01 N hydrochloric acid solution used to neutralize the extract from J(J g of glass powder minus the titration of the blank. The titre value shall not exceed J-0 mi.

APPENDIX D

( Clause 6.1 )
DETERMINATION OF DELIVERY TIME 1).1. DELIVEl\Y TIME
0.1.1 Delive.,p' time is the time taken by the descent of the water from the graduation mark to the point at which it comes to rest in the tip when , the pipette is held vertically and the tip is in contact with the inside of a b'eaker or any other suitable glass vessel.

B-1.2 For determiDiDI the delivery time clamp the pipette in a vertical poIitiOD, fill with water and set on the graduation mark. Place a beaker beneath the pipette and incline slightly 10 that the tip of the jet of the pipette ill in contact with the inside/of the beaker. Remove the finger from the top of the pipette and; simultaneously atart a stop-watch. Observe the motion of the meniscus down the pipette. The time recorded by the atop-watch "p to the period when the meniscus stops descending lliall be the delivery time of the pipette.
